title: Configure a department and protect access

scenes.title: Configure a department and protect access
scenes.narration: Welcome to Resgrid Academy. In this lesson, we will configure a department and protect access. Wrong time zones distort schedules, and broad permissions expose work to people who do not need it. We will explain the features, the setup decisions, and a practical way to check the result.

scenes.title: A department scenario
scenes.narration: An administrator sets the department time zone, hides modules the department will not use, requires two-factor sign-in for administrators and adds a second administrator. Sets the time zone and address everything else uses, and keeps administrative access limited and recoverable. The examples in this series use a fictional department and are teaching scenarios, not default settings.

scenes.title: Department Settings
scenes.narration: Department Settings. Department address, time zone and core settings. Confirm the address and time zone; dates, maps and schedules depend on them.

scenes.title: Module settings
scenes.narration: Module settings. Turn optional modules on or off for the department. Hide modules you will not use so members see a simpler menu.

scenes.title: Permissions
scenes.narration: Permissions. Who can create calls, see personal information and perform other sensitive actions. Review each permission; some default to every member.

scenes.title: Two-Factor Authentication
scenes.narration: Two-Factor Authentication. Two-factor sign-in for member accounts. Enroll every administrator in two-factor sign-in.

scenes.title: Security and session policy
scenes.narration: Security and session policy. Two-factor requirements, password rules and session limits. Require two-factor sign-in for administrators and review password and session rules.

scenes.title: Single sign-on and provisioning
scenes.narration: Single sign-on and provisioning. Let members sign in through your identity provider, with optional automatic account provisioning. Know your department address and time zone, and choose at least two people who will administer Resgrid.

scenes.title: Audit history
scenes.narration: Audit history. See who changed department settings and when. Know your department address and time zone, and choose at least two people who will administer Resgrid.

scenes.title: Account sessions and recovery
scenes.narration: Account sessions and recovery. Your own sign-in sessions, password and two-factor settings. Know your department address and time zone, and choose at least two people who will administer Resgrid.

scenes.title: Setup help and support
scenes.narration: Setup help and support. Setup Wizard, Setup Report and Admin Assist. Know your department address and time zone, and choose at least two people who will administer Resgrid.

scenes.title: Passkeys and account recovery
scenes.narration: Passkeys add a device-backed sign-in factor and need deliberate naming, removal, and recovery handling. Enroll from account security on a compatible demo device. Name the credential and review the remaining recovery factors. Confirm an actual sign-in and check the credential list after a controlled removal. Confirm availability in the demo department before recording the live workflow.

scenes.title: Configure one useful workflow
scenes.narration: For the training scenario, work in this order. Step 1. Confirm the department address and time zone. Step 2. Choose the modules the department will use and review permissions. Step 3. Enroll two administrators in MFA before reviewing enforcement and recovery.

scenes.title: Verify the result
scenes.narration: Now verify the result. Use separate administrator and member accounts to check allowed actions and resource visibility. Test recovery before enforcing stricter sign-in rules. A common problem to watch for: Hiding a module is not evidence that API access stops. MFA enrollment is separate from a tested factor and recovery path.

scenes.title: Try it with your department
scenes.narration: Your practice task is simple. Complete Setup Wizard, save on each owning screen, then Verify again. Keep unknown checks visible and assign follow-up owners. Record the result, who owns the follow-up, and when it should be reviewed.
